item.title: Dr Lalabalavu urges responsible drinking, warns of risks of unprotected sex resulting in HIV
item.description: People are being urged to drink responsibly as alcohol intoxication can lead to risky sexual behaviour that increases the risk of HIV transmission. item.content:encoded:
People are being urged to drink responsibly as alcohol intoxication can lead to risky sexual behaviour that increases the risk of HIV transmission.

While responding to questions by fijivillage News following concerns relating to unprotected sex and alcohol as a contributing factor, Minister for Health Dr Ratu Atonio Lalabalavu says alcohol itself is not the issue, but the behaviour that can follow when people become intoxicated.

Dr Lalabalavu says people who are drinking should enjoy themselves responsibly as intoxication can lead to unprotected sex and increase the risk of HIV transmission.

He says the Government is also working with the Vanua, faith-based organisations and other stakeholders to address stigma and discrimination surrounding HIV.

Dr Lalabalavu says continued awareness will remain part of the Ministry's outreach programmes.

Meanwhile, Chairman of Fiji’s National HIV Outbreak and Cluster Response Taskforce Dr Jason Mitchell says the Vanua and faith-based organisations have an important role to play because they are connected to a large part of Fiji’s population.

Dr Mitchell says increased media coverage has led to a tendency for people to turn on communities affected by HIV.

He stresses that Fiji needs an environment where people feel safe, protected and supported to access testing, treatment and care, and says we cannot afford to have a ‘vigilante approach’ to HIV on social media.

Dr Mitchell says he will ask the Cabinet subcommittee to ensure the HIV Board starts exercising its powers under the HIV Act relating to stigma, discrimination and privacy.

He says there are strong provisions under the Act and Fiji has reached a point where authorities need to say “enough is enough” and that stigma and discrimination will not be tolerated.

Dr Mitchell says this is important because stigma and discrimination could discourage people from accessing HIV services that have been made available to them.

He highlights children and adolescents are particularly vulnerable to the effects of stigma and discrimination, particularly when parents and other community members are unable or unwilling to access available services because of fear of discrimination.

While responding to questions by fijivillage News on people potentially turning to traditional or bush medicine following the declaration of HIV as a national crisis, Dr Lalabalavu says this is another area where the involvement of the Vanua and faith-based organisations will be important.

He says the issue will continue to be discussed at committee level and with the Vanua, faith-based organisations and other partners as part of Fiji’s response to the HIV crisis.

item.title: Father Law Home appeals for help with only two months of funding remaining
item.description: Father Law Home is appealing to the public for support for its 30 elderly residents as it only has enough funding to operate for another two months. The Home says it needs about $25,000 a month to care for its residents and cover essential expenses, including food, water, electricity, supplies, transport and staff wages.
item.content:encoded:
Father Law Home is appealing to the public for support for its 30 elderly residents as it only has enough funding to operate for another two months.

The Home says it needs about $25,000 a month to care for its residents and cover essential expenses, including food, water, electricity, supplies, transport and staff wages.

It says without continued financial support, it will become increasingly difficult to maintain the current level of care for residents in the coming months.

Father Law Home relies heavily on donations from individuals and organisations to continue its operations.

The Home is asking those who are able to help to make a contribution, saying even a small donation can assist with meals, essential supplies and the daily care of residents.

Father Law Home says community support will be important in keeping the Home operating and ensuring its 30 elderly residents continue to receive the care they need.

Those who would like to support Father Law Home can make a donation through its ANZ bank account.

The account number is 1319673, the BSB is 10890 and the SWIFT Code is ANZBFJFX.

item.title: Nasinu Town Council to remove abandoned vehicles, owners face costs and court action
item.description: Residents in the Laucala Industrial Area have raised safety concerns over damaged and abandoned vehicles parked along roads and public spaces, with the Nasinu Town Council planning to remove the vehicles and take action against their owners. Nasinu Town Council CEO Felix Magnus says they will issue notices to the owners requiring them to remove the vehicles.
item.content:encoded:
Residents in the Laucala Industrial Area have raised safety concerns over damaged and abandoned vehicles parked along roads and public spaces, with the Nasinu Town Council planning to remove the vehicles and take action against their owners.

Nasinu Town Council CEO Felix Magnus says they will issue notices to the owners requiring them to remove the vehicles.

He says owners will have 30 days to remove the vehicles, after which the matter will be taken to court.

Magnus says the council will sign a Memorandum of Understanding with the Land Transport Authority to share data and use LTA regulations to empower council officers on the ground.

He says the council will then proceed with the removal of the abandoned and damaged vehicles.

Magnus says the council will also approach the Ministry of Environment to determine whether the vehicles can be taken to the Naboro Landfill.

He says the costs for removing the vehicles will be charged to their owners, with LTA assisting in identifying the owners and recovering the charges when they renew their vehicle licences.

Magnus says some vehicle owners leave the vehicles at night and disappear.

He says the council can track the owners through the engine serial numbers or licence plates if they are still attached to the vehicles.

item.title: Gau resident calls for road repairs as poor conditions disrupt weekly freight service
item.description: Akariva Vura, who is originally from Nacavanadi Village, says he operates a weekly freight service for villages and settlements around Gau. Vura says he transports hardware materials, groceries and personal belongings to the island every week, making reliable road access important for families and businesses that depend on the service.
item.content:encoded:
Akariva Vura, who is originally from Nacavanadi Village, says he operates a weekly freight service for villages and settlements around Gau.

Vura says he transports hardware materials, groceries and personal belongings to the island every week, making reliable road access important for families and businesses that depend on the service.

However, he says his truck has been unable to reach some areas in recent weeks because sections of the road have become difficult to use.

Vura says heavy trucks transporting harvested pine from Narocake towards Nawaikama have contributed to damage along parts of the road.

Insert: Vura on road conditions 15th Sep, 26

He says sections of the road have become slippery and developed a number of potholes, making it difficult for his truck to travel through some areas.

Vura says he raised the issue with the Fiji Roads Authority about three weeks ago and requested that the road be upgraded.

He says reliable roads are becoming increasingly important as development continues on Gau and more vehicles and trucks are being used on the island.

Vura is calling on the Fiji Roads Authority to carry out further repair and maintenance work so freight services and residents can reliably access communities around the island.
